annotations.title: Attach a photo link to a flood observation

description:
Attach a photo to a flood observation as a reference LINK (never a file).

MCP never uploads photo bytes. A local path, file:// URL or data: URI is
refused: to upload a photo file, open the observation in the map and use the
photo strip on its form (JPEG, PNG or HEIC, 25 MB, 10 per observation).
The link counts toward the 10.

caption.description: What the photo shows (optional, up to 500 characters)

credit.description: Who took it / the rights holder (optional)

public_consent.description: Show this photo to visitors of a public project (default false: members only)

reference_url.description: An http(s) link to the photo (stored, never fetched)

name: add_observation_photo_link
title: Attach a photo link to a flood observation

annotations.title: Add flood observations to a layer

description:
Add flood observations (Flood mark, Timed level, Gauge record, Dry point) to a layer.

POSTs each observation to /projects/<id>/flood-observations/<layer>/observations/
in order. The API validates every field: a row it refuses (400) is listed in
`rejected` with its `problems` and the rest still land; a refusal that is not
about the row (403 not an Editor, 404, 409) stops the batch and is reported in
`stopped`, with `not_sent_count`. Stages are on the LAYER's vertical datum.
Photos are not part of an observation: attach a link with add_observation_photo_link.

entry_timezone.description: IANA zone for naive observed_start/observed_end on rows that do not carry their own entry_timezone; omit to use the project's zone (derived from where the project is, reported back as entry_timezone). Give it only when the times were read elsewhere

layer_id.description: The flood observation layer id (create_observation_layer / list_observations)

observations.description: Observations, each the API write body: subtype (flood_mark | timed_level | gauge_record | dry_point), name (required: a short label, e.g. the survey mark id), geometry {type: Point, coordinates: [lon, lat]} (or native x/y with srid), value_kind (stage | depth) + stage_m or depth_m, uncertainty_grade (H/M/L) or uncertainty_m, bound (exact | at_least | at_most), observed_start/observed_end (ISO 8601; naive times read in entry_timezone, by default the project's own zone), mark_type, flood_name, source, licence, notes; a flood_mark or dry_point must say which flood it is: a date window (observed_start / observed_end) or flood_name (ask the user; never guess a date); a gauge_record needs data_timeseries_id (+ gauge_zero_m). At most 200 per call

srid.description: EPSG code for every geometry that does not carry its own `srid` (the projected CRS its eastings/northings are in, e.g. a UTM zone); omit for [lon, lat] (EPSG:4326)

name: add_observations
title: Add flood observations to a layer

annotations.title: Attach an uploaded layer as a project input

description:
Attach a GeoJSON you uploaded to GeoNode as the project's boundary, friction, inflow, rainfall, building, mesh_region or culvert layer.

Only for a client that has a shell and an agent key. A connector agent
with no shell (claude.ai) writes the layer inline with write_input_layer,
or, for a file above the inline cap, gives the user the
request_input_upload link instead.

The agent moves the bytes: first upload the GeoJSON yourself, with the
same agent key, to GeoNode's upload endpoint at the site origin:

    curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer hk_...' -F "base_file=@/path/rainfall.geojson" https://<site>/api/v2/uploads/upload/

→ JSON with `execution_id`. Then call this tool with it. The tool polls
GET /api/v2/resource-service/execution-status/<execution_id> (bounded by
timeout_seconds; statuses ready → running → finished | failed), reads the
new dataset's pk, and PATCHes it onto the project's DEFAULT row of that
kind ('Boundary 01' … 'MeshRegion 01' — the six rows the terrain import
seeds ~30 s after get_terrain reports ready; if the list is still empty
the tool says so: run finalize_terrain_upload / wait for get_terrain first).

kind `culvert` (Hydraulic Structures; one two-point line per culvert,
Inlet first, then Outlet): no culvert row is seeded by the terrain import,
so a project with none answers `no_default_row`: write the culverts with
write_input_layer, which makes the row. Hydrata converts every attached
layer into the project's grid and the kind's table shape (single
geometries, the_geom, the kind's own columns); attribute names are matched
as they are, nothing is renamed for you (see write_input_layer).
The culvert engine conveys flow through each culvert in a run (GPU
lanes and localhost; the multi-core CPU lanes refuse a culvert scenario).

`outcome` is exactly one of: `attached` (row_id, gn_layer, dataset_pk and
dataset_alternate — the WFS typename — of the CONVERTED layer the row now
uses, source_dataset_pk — the dataset you uploaded — and every row id seen);
`timed_out` (still importing: call
again with the same arguments, except pass `retry_execution_id` as
execution_id when the result carries one); `upload_failed` (the
execution record, incl. its log, is returned verbatim — fix the file and
upload again); `no_default_row`; `no_dataset` (finished but no resource
was recorded). The PATCH is refused with a 400 if the dataset is not
owned by you.

Every layer attached here is marked as written by your agent key and is
UNREVIEWED until the user reviews it in their browser (the build refuses
UNREVIEWED_INPUTS until then). INFLOWS: never invent an inflow location —
no coordinates you made up, guessed or "placed plausibly". Import the
location from the study's own files, or give the user the ui_url to draw
it in the map; say in say_to_user that the inflow is unreviewed and where
they check or draw it.

Refused, with no request made: kind `breakline` — no REST create path
exists for it at HEAD (TASK-3040 AC6), so attaching one would only
pretend. Also refused without a request: an execution_id that is not the
UUID the upload returned.
One GeoJSON per kind: all of a kind's features travel in that one file. A
rainfall polygon names its gauge in its `data` property — create that
gauge with create_time_series under the exact same name.

execution_id.description: `execution_id` returned by your multipart POST to <origin>/api/v2/uploads/upload/

kind.description: Which input the uploaded layer is: boundary, friction, inflow, rainfall, building, mesh_region or culvert ('structure' is a deprecated alias of building). breakline is refused (see below).

timeout_seconds.description: How long this call keeps polling the upload before it returns `timed_out` (default 180, ceiling 200 — claude.ai cuts a tool call at 240 s). 0 = one status read, no waiting.

name: attach_input_layer
title: Attach an uploaded layer as a project input

annotations.title: Build a scenario's mesh and package

description:
Build a scenario's package (mesh + inputs) after showing what it will cost, and poll until built.

Needs a launch-level agent key (a build can start AWS Batch); a read or
draft key gets 403 AGENT_LEVEL_INSUFFICIENT — the user creates a launch key
on the site's Agent keys page (/agents/).

Order of operations, so the number is shown before anything is spent:

1. GET the scenario detail. A record with no `boundary`/`computed_status`
   keys is a non-member's read of a public project → refused: a build
   needs the EDITOR role.
2. Re-call checks on `latest_run` (a re-POST is NOT deduplicated after
   `built`/`complete` — it would dispatch a duplicate build): no run →
   proceed; run `created`/`building` → resume polling, no POST; run
   `built`/`queued`/`computing`/`processing`/`complete` with
   `latest_run_is_valid` not false → return that state, no POST unless
   rebuild=true; run `error`/`cancelled`, or `latest_run_is_valid` false
   (the scenario was edited since the build) → proceed.
3. Spend gates, each a refusal with `outcome: "refused"` and no POST: the
   scenario has no boundary or its boundary row has no features (the
   server would admit the build and fail it in make_package); the
   estimate is None (resolution is 0/unset); the estimate is above
   100,000 triangles and confirm is not true — the refusal states the
   number; re-call with confirm=true to proceed. An estimate of 0 over a
   boundary WITH features is buildable and is reported, not refused.
4. POST /projects/<id>/scenarios/<pk>/build/. Every 4xx comes back
   verbatim as a normal result with `http_status`: 422 MESH_TOO_LARGE
   (`error_code`, `estimate`, `ceiling`, `detail` — the server's hard
   ceiling; coarsen `resolution` or shrink the boundary; no run was
   created), 409 COMPUTE_TARGET_UNAVAILABLE, 400/403/404. 409
   UNREVIEWED_INPUTS (inputs you wrote that the user has not reviewed)
   answers `outcome` `unreviewed_inputs` with the `unreviewed_inputs` list and a
   `ui_url` to the scenario's review screen: give the user the link, poll
   get_scenario until its `unreviewed_inputs` is empty, then build again. A 409 WITHOUT
   an error_code is the dedup body ({status, run_id, detail}: a build is
   already in flight) — the tool resumes polling that run.
5. On 202 poll the detail's `computed_status` (created → building →
   built | error), bounded by timeout_seconds.

Returns a COMPACT state, never the whole detail: `outcome` (built, error,
cancelled, complete/queued/computing/processing for a run past the build,
timed_out, or refused), `computed_status`, `mesh_triangle_count_estimate`,
`posted`, the POST's `build` body + `http_status` when one was made, and
the latest run's `run_id`, `run_status`, `error_message`, `user_message`,
`mesh_triangle_count`. `timed_out` is normal (make_package re-downloads
the terrain from S3 every build; minutes): call again with the same
arguments — step 2 resumes polling the same run, it never POSTs twice —
or cancel_run(run_id) if the run is stuck in `created` with no worker.
`error` is terminal: `error_message` says why (fix the inputs, then call
again — an errored latest run is rebuilt).

Units: `resolution` — on the SCENARIO and on every MeshRegion FEATURE — is
a LENGTH in metres; ANUGA maximum_triangle_area = resolution²/2 (FloatField
default 100, not nullable; 0 makes the estimate None), and the estimate
prices both the same way (TASK-3186). The smallest value becomes the raster
cell size. A MeshRegion feature must carry `resolution_units = m` (features
drawn in the map are marked automatically); an unmarked one makes the build
answer 422 MESH_REGION_UNITS_UNMARKED, naming the conversion an operator runs.

confirm.description: Required (true) when the estimate is above 100,000 triangles — the tool refuses first and tells you the number. Default false.

rebuild.description: true to dispatch a NEW build of a scenario whose latest run is already built/complete and still valid (default false: the tool returns that state instead of duplicating the build).

timeout_seconds.description: How long this call keeps polling before it returns `timed_out` (default 180, ceiling 200 — claude.ai cuts a tool call at 240 s). 0 = one status read, no waiting.

name: build_scenario
title: Build a scenario's mesh and package

description:
Cancel an in-flight simulation run.

Needs a launch-level agent key; a read or draft key gets 403
AGENT_LEVEL_INSUFFICIENT.

Works on runs in built, queued, or computing status. Cleans up
compute resources (terminates EC2 instance, Celery task, or Batch job).

Returns 409 if the run is already in a terminal state
(complete, cancelled, or error).
name: cancel_run
title: Cancel a run

description:
Create a flood observation layer in a project and wait for its map layer.

A flood observation layer holds real flood evidence (Flood marks, Timed
levels, Gauge records, Dry points) that every historic run is compared
with (Compare with observations). It is project-level: it is never a scenario input.
POSTs /projects/<id>/flood-observations/, then polls the layer until its
GeoServer layer exists (`ready`), usually a few seconds; until then
add_observations refuses. On `timed_out`, call list_observations later.

datum_offset_m.description: Metres ADDED to every stage on the layer to bring it onto the terrain datum. Required for vertical_datum=local; null means 0 otherwise

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the map layer (clamped to 200)

vertical_datum.description: The datum the layer's stages are on: terrain (default, 'Same as terrain'), local ('Local datum (constant offset)', needs datum_offset_m), or the vertical datum the levels were surveyed on: an EPSG vertical CRS (e.g. 'EPSG:5703') or the datum's own name (at most 32 characters). Ask the user; never assume one from the country

name: create_observation_layer
title: Create a flood observation layer

description:
Create a new ANUGA project. Returns the project record including its id, base_map and ui_url.

The caller's own account becomes the owner. `projection` is the projected
CRS every scenario in the project is meshed and run in — pick the UTM zone
covering the site. The project's map is created alongside it; `ui_url`
opens it — give it to the user. A project you create is unpublished
(`is_published: false`): only its owner and members can see it until the
user presses Publish in its Sharing panel in the browser — you cannot
publish it. Next step for a new project: presign_terrain_upload.

projection.description: Working CRS as an EPSG string, normally the UTM zone of the site, e.g. 'EPSG:32756' (WGS 84 / UTM 56S)

name: create_project
title: Create a project

description:
Create a DRAFT scenario (no build, no run) and report its mesh-triangle estimate.

POSTs /projects/<id>/scenarios/ with the write fields, then GETs the
scenario detail — the create response carries NO estimate; the detail's
`mesh_triangle_count_estimate` (+ `_breakdown`) does. Returns a compact
record (the same fields get_scenario answers with): id, name, the FK ids
as stored, resolution, duration, `computed_status` (`created` = no run
yet), the estimate and its breakdown, the price (`compute_cost_estimate`
in USD, `vcpu_hours_estimate`), `inflow_anchor_mismatch`, and
http_status. Next step: build_scenario (which asks for
confirm=true above 100,000 triangles). Nothing is meshed or queued here.

Units: `resolution` — on the SCENARIO and on every MeshRegion FEATURE — is
a LENGTH in metres; ANUGA maximum_triangle_area = resolution²/2 (FloatField
default 100, not nullable; 0 makes the estimate None), and the estimate
prices both the same way (TASK-3186). The smallest value becomes the raster
cell size. A MeshRegion feature must carry `resolution_units = m` (features
drawn in the map are marked automatically); an unmarked one makes the build
answer 422 MESH_REGION_UNITS_UNMARKED, naming the conversion an operator runs.

The server does NOT validate that the FK ids belong to `project_id` —
pass the row ids attach_input_layer / get_terrain returned for THIS
project. Every FK is nullable at create time, and the build fails later
on a scenario with no terrain, or with neither an inflow nor a rainfall.
A `boundary` whose row has no features (the default 'Boundary 01' before
attach_input_layer) is accepted here and refused by build_scenario. The
estimate is None when resolution is 0; an estimate of 0 with a real
boundary is a very coarse mesh, not an error.

culvert.description: Culvert row id (optional; attach_input_layer kind=culvert → row_id). The build refuses a culvert missing its shape, size or invert levels.

inflow.description: Inflow row id (optional; the build needs an inflow OR a rainfall)

mesh_region.description: MeshRegion row id (optional): finer meshing inside its polygons, each feature's `resolution` a LENGTH in metres (see the units note).

rainfall.description: Rainfall row id (optional; the build needs an inflow OR a rainfall)

resolution.description: Mesh resolution as a LENGTH in metres (ANUGA maximum_triangle_area = resolution²/2). Coarser (larger) = fewer triangles: on a ~13 km² boundary 36-40 m gives ~16-20k triangles, 10 m ~255k, 1 m ~25M (refused by the API).

structure.description: Deprecated alias of `building` (TASK-3586); ignored when `building` is given.

terrain.description: Terrain id (get_terrain → terrain.id); the build fails without one

name: create_scenario
title: Create a draft scenario

annotations.title: Fetch terrain from a Hydrata source

description:
Have Hydrata fetch a terrain from one of its own sources, then wait for the import (like get_terrain).

Use a `key` from list_terrain_sources. Hydrata fetches, reprojects and publishes the
DEM and seeds the project's default input rows; the DEM's datum is stamped by the source.
The result is get_terrain's envelope (`outcome` ready | error | timed_out, `terrain`,
`polls`) plus `terrain_source`: the source's `key`, `name`, `resolution_m`, `licence`,
`credit` and `vertical_datum`. `timed_out` is normal for a large area: keep calling
get_terrain(project_id, terrain_id). A refusal (the box is over the source's size cap,
the source has no data there, an unknown source) comes back as `outcome: refused`
with the reason in `say_to_user` and nothing is created.

bbox.description: The site as [min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat] in WGS84 degrees

project_id.description: The project ID (the key needs Contributor rights; a launch-level key since the import can start AWS Batch)

source.description: A source `key` from list_terrain_sources, e.g. `ga_lidar_5m` or `copernicus_glo30`

timeout_seconds.description: How long this call keeps polling the import before it returns `timed_out` (default 180, ceiling 200). 0 = start it and return at once; then call get_terrain.

title.description: Terrain title (default: the source name and box)

name: create_terrain_from_source
title: Fetch terrain from a Hydrata source

description:
Create a time series (rain gauge, hydrograph, tide/stage) in a project.

POSTs /projects/<id>/time-series/ with `series_type` and `units` as
top-level fields. `series_type` is checked against the four choices and
`data` against the {"rowData": [{timestamp, value}, ...]} shape before any
request is made — the API answers 500 (not 400) to a malformed row.
Returns a compact record — id, name, series_type, units, timezone,
row_count, http_status — not the echoed rows; fetch the full row with the
REST API (GET /projects/<id>/time-series/<id>/) if you need to round-trip it.
A rainfall polygon references its gauge by the series NAME, so create the
gauges with the exact names the rainfall GeoJSON's features carry.

The units must match the series_type (see `units`), and a hydrograph or
hyetograph must END at 0 unless `hold_last_value` is true. The result
carries Hydrata's own `summary` of the series (peak, volume or depth,
first and last stamp, trailing value): repeat those numbers to the user
(`say_to_user` does) rather than computing your own.

data.description: The rows: {"rowData": [{"timestamp": "1998-08-17T00:00:00", "value": 1.5}, ...]}. Timestamps ISO 8601 (a trailing Z is tolerated), values numeric. Validated here before anything is sent.

hold_last_value.description: Set true ONLY when the last value is meant to be held after the series ends. A hydrograph or hyetograph whose last value is not 0 is refused (TRAILING_VALUE_HELD) unless this is true: end the series with a 0 row instead, unless holding is really intended.

method.description: One short phrase saying how you got these numbers (e.g. 'read off the council hydrograph PDF', 'scaled the 1% AEP peak'). Shown to the person who reviews the inputs.

name.description: Series name, kept VERBATIM — a rainfall polygon binds to its gauge by this exact name (its `data` property), so use the name the GeoJSON features carry

series_type.description: One of hyetograph (rainfall depth/intensity — the default), hydrograph (flow, read by the Hydrographs panel and inflow boundaries), stage (water level, e.g. a tide) or generic. Sent as a top-level field.

source.description: Where the data came from, e.g. a gauge id or agency (optional)

timezone.description: IANA timezone of the timestamps (default 'UTC'), e.g. 'Australia/Sydney'

units.description: Units of the values. REQUIRED for hyetograph ('mm/hr' or 'mm/h'), hydrograph ('m3/s', 'm^3/s' or 'cumec') and stage ('m'): the engine reads those units whatever the label says, so a mismatch is refused before anything is sent. Free for generic.

name: create_time_series
title: Create a time series

description:
Delete one flood observation and its photos (cannot be undone).

DELETEs /projects/<id>/flood-observations/<layer>/observations/<fid>/; a
missing fid is an error (404), not a silent success.
name: delete_observation
title: Delete one flood observation

description:
Delete a time series (cannot be undone). Needs the Manager role on the project.

A series still used by a feature of an inflow, rainfall or boundary layer is
refused (409) and the refusal names the layer and the feature that use it:
detach it there (or point that feature at another series), then call again.
A series that no feature uses is deleted.
name: delete_time_series
title: Delete a time series

description:
Say what each input layer kind looks like: geometry, properties, allowed values, a minimal example.

Read this BEFORE you build GeoJSON for write_input_layer or an upload. Per kind it
returns the `geometry` (LineString or Polygon), every property the layer reads with its
`type`, whether it is `required` and its `allowed` values or `min`/`max`, the
`required_one_of` groups (an inflow needs data_constant or data_timeseries_id), `notes`
in plain words and a minimal `example` FeatureCollection. It is generated by Hydrata from
the same definitions the build reads, so it is never out of date: do not read source code
or guess column names.

kind.description: One kind to describe (boundary, friction, inflow, rainfall, building, mesh_region or culvert); empty describes all seven

name: describe_input_kinds
title: Describe the input layer formats

description:
Step 2 of a terrain import: register the PUT GeoTIFF as a Terrain and start the import.

Needs a launch-level agent key (the import can start AWS Batch); a read or
draft key gets 403 AGENT_LEVEL_INSUFFICIENT — the user creates a launch key
on the site's Agent keys page (/agents/).

Call this only after the presigned PUT returned 200. Creates the Terrain row
(status `creating`) and queues the import chain — reproject to UTM, publish
the layer + hillshade, style — which also seeds the project's six default
boundary, friction, inflow, rainfall, building and mesh-region rows.
Returns 202 with the terrain record; keep its `id` for get_terrain. A 400 UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND
means no object is at `staging_key`: the PUT did not land (check its status
code and Content-Type) — do not retry finalize until it has.

process_id.description: `process_id` returned by presign_terrain_upload (pass it so the upload's progress record is reused; the API tolerates its absence)

vertical_datum_declared.description: TASK-4061: the datum the user SAYS the heights are on: `ahd` (Australian Height Datum), `orthometric_egm2008` or `ellipsoid`. Pass it only when the user told you; if they did not, ask them, do not guess. Stored as the terrain's declared datum, which beats Hydrata's own inference. Omit when unknown.

name: finalize_terrain_upload
title: Register an uploaded terrain

annotations.title: Compare a run with flood observations

description:
Compare a run with the project's flood observations: how well does it match them?

Returns `headline` (the figures to tell the user, e.g. "47 observations · 31
within ±0.30 m (66%) · bias -0.12 m · RMSE 0.35 m · 1 excluded"),
`headline_numbers` (the same as numbers), `tolerance_m` (used) and
`default_tolerance_m` (the project's saved one), `statistics`
(the API's summary: n, within, within_pct, bias_m, rmse_m, weighted_rmse_m, mae_m, max_abs_m,
excluded, not_scored by reason, gauges), `gauges` (Gauge records: peak error,
timing error, NSE), `datum_checks` (warn the user only when `warning` is true:
both datums known and different; `not_recorded` = the terrain has no
recorded datum, stated in `note`, not a warning)
and one row per observation: observed_m / modelled_m / residual_m (modelled -
observed, + = model high), within, scored / not_scored_reason, match
(`outside_run_window` = not this flood), excluded + exclusion {reason, by, at}.
`sampling` counts how the modelled values were read: `centroid` (the peak
of the mesh triangle the observation sits in), `nearest_node_fallback` (an
older run without that peak: the nearest mesh node's value, tell the user)
and `nearest_node` (just outside the mesh); each row's `sample.method` says
which.
There is no pass or fail: report the figures. A run that is not historic has
none (`has_comparison` false) — do not retry it.

include_series.description: Keep each Gauge record's modelled stage series (every saved frame); default false

layer_id.description: With fid: narrow the rows to ONE flood observation and add its history

run_id.description: The run ID (a historic run; others are not compared with observations)

tolerance.description: Metres within which a residual counts as within (default: the project's saved tolerance, 0.3 unless an Editor changed it; presets 0.15, 0.3, 0.4; above 0 and at most 5). Not stored: it only changes this answer

name: get_observation_comparison
title: Compare a run with flood observations

annotations.title: Get a project and its map link

description:
Get one ANUGA project: id, name, projection, visibility, your role, its base map — and the link to it.

Returns the project record (`id`, `name`, `projection` (EPSG code),
`simple_view_config`, `visibility`, `owner_username`, `my_role`,
`base_map`) plus `ui_url`: the link that opens the project's map, for the
user (`<site>/catalogue/#/map/<base_map>`; null while a new project's map
is still being created). Scenarios are NOT listed here — use get_scenario
with a scenario id.
name: get_project
title: Get a project and its map link

description:
Get full details of a simulation run including timing and results.

Returns the complete run record: status, progress, timing (start/end
timestamps, duration), compute details (backend, instance type, cost),
mesh info, error messages, and result log. Use get_run_status for
lightweight polling; use this for final results.

The presigned `s3_*_url` download links are ELIDED — each is a 6-hour
capability and no tool relays one. The results stay viewable through the
`gn_layer_*` entries (published WMS layers on the project's map).

`sww` reports the run's full time series (the raw ANUGA output): `state`
(available, not_kept, archived or restoring), `size_bytes`, and a `ui_url`
to the Results panel where the person downloads it (or requests a restore
of an archived one and is emailed when it is ready). The download link
itself is never returned.
name: get_run
title: Get a run's full record

description:
Lightweight status check for a simulation run (fast, <50ms).

Use this for polling instead of get_run. Returns only: id, status,
`phase`, progress_pct (0-100), eta_seconds, error_message, and
compute_backend.

`phase` is never empty: it is `status`, except `preparing_inputs` while a
`computing` run has no progress yet (it is downloading its input package
and building the domain — minutes on a big model; this is NOT a stall).
Poll every 5-10 seconds. Terminal states: complete, error, cancelled.
name: get_run_status
title: Poll a run's status

annotations.title: Get a scenario's state, inputs and price

description:
Get a scenario's COMPACT state: its `computed_status`, inputs, estimate and price.

Returns a compact record, never the raw ~50 KB detail: `scenario_id`,
`computed_status`, `mesh_triangle_count_estimate` and its `_breakdown`,
`latest_run_is_valid`, the latest run's `run_id`, `run_status`,
`error_message`, `user_message`, `status_detail` and `mesh_triangle_count`
— plus what the scenario IS and what it will cost: `name`, `description`,
`project`, `resolution`, `duration`, the input row ids (`terrain`,
`boundary`, `friction`, `inflow`, `rainfall`, `building`, `mesh_region`, `culvert`),
`compute_cost_estimate` (USD), `vcpu_hours_estimate`, and
`inflow_anchor_mismatch` (null unless an inflow series starts after the
model does: the model gets zero flow from that series over the lead-in
gap before its first sample), and
`hydrology_check` (when Hydrata sends it: for each inflow and rainfall
feature, the series that drives it, its peak and volume, and structured
warnings — repeat those numbers to the user, never your own), and
`unbound_series` with a `say_to_user` warning when the project holds a
rainfall or flow series that no inflow or rainfall feature uses (the model
ignores it: tell the user and ask which input it belongs to).

The `computed_status` field (there is NO `status` key on a scenario) is
derived from the latest run and will be one of: created, building, built,
queued, computing, processing, complete, error, or cancelled — `created`
also means no run exists yet. A scenario must be `built` before it can be
run. `latest_run_is_valid` is false after any edit since the last build.
`unreviewed_inputs` lists the inputs written by an agent key that the user
has not reviewed at their current content (kind, layer_id, title,
feature_count, the grant that wrote it, `authored_method` (the agent's own account of
how it made the input, when it gave one), `reopened` when an edit undid an
earlier input review): while it is not empty, build and run are refused
UNREVIEWED_INPUTS. Only the user reviews, in the browser — poll this tool
every 30-60 s after giving them the review link.
A non-member reading a public project's scenario gets a reduced record:
the fields the server withholds (the input ids, the price,
`inflow_anchor_mismatch`) are ABSENT here rather than reported as null —
"withheld" is not "no terrain, no cost" — while the run-state keys,
`computed_status` among them, read null.

No presigned S3 URL is returned by any read tool (each is a 6-hour
capability): results stay viewable through a run's `gn_layer_*` WMS
entries — use get_run for the full run record.
name: get_scenario
title: Get a scenario's state, inputs and price

description:
Poll a terrain's import until it is `ready` (or `error`), bounded by timeout_seconds.

Returns `outcome` — exactly one of `ready`, `error`, `timed_out`, `not_found`
(the project has no terrain yet; an unknown terrain_id is an API 404 error
instead) — plus the last `status` seen (creating → styling → ready | error)
and `phase` (that status, or `not_found`; never empty),
`polls`, `elapsed_seconds` and the full `terrain` record (its `gn_layer` is
the published elevation dataset pk once ready). An import takes minutes to
tens of minutes (the SAME 32 MB 1 m DEM measured 4.5 min once and 26 min
once — the worker's S3 download speed dominates), so `timed_out` is normal
and NOT a failure: keep calling with the same arguments while `status` is
still `creating`/`styling`; several calls in a row is expected. `error` is
terminal — the import failed and no default input rows were seeded; upload
a corrected GeoTIFF as a new terrain.

`ready` is written by the import task; the project's default input rows
(Boundary 01, Friction 01, Inflow 01, Rainfall 01, Building 01,
MeshRegion 01, one GeoNode layer each) are seeded by the NEXT task in the
chain and appear over the following ~30 s. Poll the input-layer list until
it is non-empty before attaching your own layer to a default row.

terrain_id.description: The terrain ID from finalize_terrain_upload. Omit to follow the project's newest terrain.

timeout_seconds.description: How long this call keeps polling before it returns `timed_out` (default 180, ceiling 200 — claude.ai cuts a tool call at 240 s). 0 = one status read, no waiting.

name: get_terrain
title: Wait for a terrain import

description:
List every input layer row of a project, per kind, with whether it has features.

For each of boundary, friction, inflow, rainfall, building, mesh_region and culvert:
the rows (`row_id`, `title`, `gn_layer` — the dataset pk — and
`dataset_alternate`, the `workspace:name` WFS typename), `authored_method`
(the one-line account an agent gave of how it made the layer; null when
nobody said) and `has_features`.
`has_features` is the API's own answer for every kind. It is null only when
a row's record does not carry it: treat null as unknown, not as empty. A row
with no `gn_layer` has no layer yet (`has_features` false). Use the row ids with
create_scenario; this is the listing primitive — no need to probe files.
name: list_inputs
title: List a project's input layers

annotations.title: List flood observation layers or observations

description:
List a project's flood observation layers, or one layer's observations.

Without layer_id: every layer (layer_id, title, dataset_alternate, vertical_datum,
datum_offset_m, has_features). With layer_id: {layer, count, results} where each
observation carries its `fid` (the key for update_observation / delete_observation),
subtype + subtype_label, stage/depth, sigma, bound, the observed window in UTC,
`datum` status (an `unknown` datum is not scored), `photo_count` and `problems`
(fields drawn in the map that fail validation, reported, never fixed).

layer_id.description: A flood observation layer id; omit to list the project's layers instead

name: list_observations
title: List flood observation layers or observations

description:
List ANUGA simulation projects accessible to the authenticated user.

Returns a paginated list of projects with their names, projections,
and base map references.
name: list_projects
title: List projects

description:
List all simulation runs across all scenarios in a project.

Returns a paginated list of runs. Optionally filter by status
to find active, completed, or failed runs. Each row's presigned
`s3_*_url` download links are elided (6-hour capabilities).

status_filter.description: Filter by status: created, building, built, queued, computing, processing, complete, error, cancelled. Omit for all.

name: list_runs
title: List a project's runs

annotations.title: List the terrain Hydrata can fetch for a site

description:
List the terrain Hydrata can fetch for a site, finest resolution first.

Ask this BEFORE fetching or uploading your own DEM. Each source row has `key`,
`name`, `resolution_m`, `coverage_pct` (share of your box it has data for),
`cap` (`state` ok | too_large, the area and the maximum, and a plain `message`
when too large), `vertical_datum`, `credit` and `licence`. Only sources with some
coverage appear: Copernicus GLO-30 (30 m, worldwide) always, and finer regional
LiDAR such as Geoscience Australia 5 m where it has data. Pick one whose `cap.state`
is ok and pass its `key` to create_terrain_from_source. Tell the user which source
you chose, its resolution, licence and datum (`say_to_user` says it for you).

bbox.description: The site as [min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat] in WGS84 degrees, e.g. [149.105, -35.285, 149.135, -35.255] for Sullivans Creek, Canberra.

project_id.description: The project ID (the key needs Contributor rights on it)

name: list_terrain_sources
title: List the terrain Hydrata can fetch for a site

description:
List a project's time series (rain gauges, hydrographs, tides) — never their rows.

Each series: `id`, `name` (a rainfall polygon binds to its gauge by this
exact name), `series_type`, `units`, `timezone`, `authored_method` (how an
agent made it; null when nobody said), `row_count`,
`first_timestamp` and `last_timestamp`. The data rows themselves are
dropped (a project's list is megabytes); fetch one series with the REST API
(GET /projects/<id>/time-series/<id>/) if you need its values.
name: list_time_series
title: List a project's time series

description:
Step 1 of a terrain import: get a presigned S3 PUT URL for a GeoTIFF DEM.

Only for a client that has a shell and an agent key AND a DEM no platform
source covers. A connector agent with no shell (claude.ai) uses
list_terrain_sources then create_terrain_from_source instead, or asks the
user to upload their own DEM in the map.

The import needs a launch-level agent key: a draft key can presign, but
finalize_terrain_upload (and the multipart fallback below) answer a read or
draft key 403 AGENT_LEVEL_INSUFFICIENT — check the key before moving bytes.

The agent moves the bytes itself — no tool accepts file contents. After this
call, PUT the file straight to `upload_url`, sending the SAME Content-Type
you passed here (it is part of the signature; a mismatch is a 403
SignatureDoesNotMatch before it is anything else):

    curl -sS -X PUT -H "Content-Type: image/tiff" --upload-file /path/dem.tif "$UPLOAD_URL"

then call finalize_terrain_upload with the returned staging_key and
process_id. Nothing exists in Hydrata until finalize; the URL expires after
`expires_in` seconds (3600).

Platform guidance: keep the terrain extent within 5° across and 40,000 km²
(200 × 200 km). The API enforces that cap on its bbox-fetch path; an
uploaded GeoTIFF is only rejected above 5 GiB, but a larger DEM will not
mesh or run well. The GeoTIFF must carry a CRS; the import reprojects it to
the site's UTM zone and builds a hillshade. Fallback when a presigned PUT is
impossible: multipart-POST the file with the same agent key to
/api/v2/anuga/projects/<id>/terrain/upload/ (form field `file`, optional
`title`), which creates the terrain in one step — then get_terrain.

content_type.description: MIME type the PUT will send (default 'image/tiff'). It is SIGNED into the URL, so the PUT must send exactly this Content-Type header.

filename.description: Base name of the GeoTIFF, e.g. 'dem.tif' (a name only — never contents)

size.description: File size in bytes (`stat -c %s <file>`). The API rejects > 5 GiB up front. Omit if unknown.

name: presign_terrain_upload
title: Get a terrain upload URL

annotations.title: Get a browser upload link for a big input layer

description:
Get the link where the PERSON uploads a big input layer in their browser.

For a layer too big to send with write_input_layer (over about 150 KB):
building footprints, land-use friction. You cannot move file bytes, so give
the person `ui_url`. It opens the project's upload page for this kind; they
drop a GeoJSON, a zipped shapefile or a GeoPackage (up to 100 MB), Hydrata
converts it into the project's grid and attaches it to the kind's layer,
replacing what it held. Nothing is created until they drop a file.

A file the person drops is their own input: it is marked 'uploaded by the
user' and needs no review step. Afterwards call list_inputs: the layer is
there with that `authored_method`. A file of the wrong kind (polygons on an
inflow) is refused on the page with a plain message. The person needs Editor
access on the project.

kind.description: Which input the file is for: boundary, friction, inflow, rainfall, building, mesh_region or culvert ('structure' is a deprecated alias of building).

name: request_input_upload
title: Get a browser upload link for a big input layer

description:
Retry a failed simulation run.

Needs a launch-level agent key (a retry rebuilds the package and can start
AWS Batch); a read or draft key gets 403 AGENT_LEVEL_INSUFFICIENT.

Starts a fresh package build of the run's scenario as a NEW run, which
becomes the scenario's latest run. The errored run keeps its status and
error as history, and the response describes that old run; the new run's
ID is get_scenario's `run_id`. Only valid when status is 'error'. Returns
409 for any other state.
name: retry_run
title: Retry a failed run

annotations.title: Save a project's default comparison tolerance

description:
Save a project's default tolerance for comparing runs with flood observations.

Needs Editor (or above). Every later get_observation_comparison (and the map's
Compare with observations tab) uses it unless a tolerance is passed. Only
save it when the user asks to change the project's default; to show the
figures at another tolerance, pass `tolerance` to get_observation_comparison.

tolerance_m.description: The project's default tolerance in metres (above 0 and at most 5; presets 0.15, 0.3, 0.4)

name: set_comparison_tolerance
title: Save a project's default comparison tolerance

annotations.title: Exclude or include a flood observation in a run's comparison

description:
Exclude a flood observation from ONE run's comparison with observations, or include it again.

Needs Editor (or above) on the project. The exclusion is logged with the user
and reason (nothing is overwritten) and keyed on (run, layer, fid), so it
survives a recompute. The figures change at once: `headline_after` is the
run's headline with the change applied. To exclude, the user must give the
reason: if they have not, ASK them; do not make one up.

excluded.description: true to exclude (default), false to include it again

reason.description: WHY the engineer excludes it, in their words (required to exclude; never invent one — ask the user). Optional when including it again

name: set_observation_exclusion
title: Exclude or include a flood observation in a run's comparison

description:
Start a flood simulation run for a built scenario.

Needs a launch-level agent key (a run spends compute); a read or draft key
gets 403 AGENT_LEVEL_INSUFFICIENT — the user creates a launch key on the
site's Agent keys page (/agents/).

The scenario must be in 'built' status. Returns 202 with the new run.
The run transitions through: built → queued → computing → processing → complete.

After starting, poll get_run_status to track progress. Returns 409
if the scenario is not in the correct state. The returned run record has
its presigned `s3_*_url` links elided (6-hour capabilities).

INPUT REVIEW (Hydrata enforces it): while an input you wrote is not reviewed by
the user, the run is not started - `outcome` `unreviewed_inputs`,
`error_code` UNREVIEWED_INPUTS, a `ui_url` to the scenario's review screen.
A run built from inputs other than the ones reviewed now answers
`outcome` `run_invalidated` (RUN_INVALIDATED): build_scenario with
rebuild=true, then start it again.

SPEND CONSENT (Hydrata enforces it; you cannot): a run whose quote does not
fit your agent key's monthly spend limit (default $0), or that Hydrata
cannot price, is NOT started. The result is then a normal (non-error)
answer with `outcome` `consent_required`, `error_code` CONSENT_REQUIRED,
`quoted_cost_usd` and `consent_url`: give the user the link and the price
(`say_to_user`). Only they can approve, in their browser. Then do NOT call
start_simulation again for this run: poll get_run_status(run_id) — the run
leaves `built` once they press the button. (With consent_timeout_seconds > 0
this call polls the run itself and answers `outcome` `consented`, with the
run, if they approve within that time.)

consent_timeout_seconds.description: When the run needs the person's consent (CONSENT_REQUIRED), how long this call keeps polling the run for their click before it returns (ceiling 200). Default 0: return the consent link at once, so you can give it to them — they cannot press a button they have not been shown.

name: start_simulation
title: Start a simulation run (spends compute)

annotations.title: Tell the Hydrata team about a capability that is missing

description:
Tell the Hydrata team about something the person asked for that NO existing tool can do.

Use it only when you have checked the other tools and none can do what the person asked
(never to report a bug, and never instead of a tool that can do it). Describe the need, not a
workaround; send no personal data, keys or file contents. It changes none of the person's data.
The reply tells you what to say: relay `say_to_user` to the person as it is. Limit: 20 a day
per person.

goal.description: What they were trying to achieve with it (optional)

what.description: What the person asked for that no tool can do, in one or two plain sentences

name: suggest_capability
title: Tell the Hydrata team about a capability that is missing

description:
Edit one flood observation (PATCH; only the fields given change).

The API checks the stored observation merged with `changes` and refuses
(400, every bad field named) rather than store a half-valid one. Photos are
not fields: attach a link with add_observation_photo_link.

changes.description: Only the fields to change, in the add_observations write shape (e.g. {"stage_m": 2.5} or a new geometry); validated by the API against the stored observation (a flood_mark or dry_point must keep a date window or a flood_name)

name: update_observation
title: Edit one flood observation

description:
Correct a time series you created (PATCH; only the fields you pass change).

Use it to fix a series instead of leaving a wrong one behind. The same
rules as create_time_series apply to new rows (units match the type, a
hydrograph or hyetograph ends at 0 unless `hold_last_value`, at least 2
rows, no negative rain or flow, not all zero) and Hydrata refuses with the
reason in plain words. A series already used by a built scenario changes the
scenario: it needs a rebuild and the user reviews it again. Returns a compact
record, not the rows.

data.description: Replacement rows: {"rowData": [{"timestamp": "<ISO 8601>", "value": <number>}, ...]}. Validated here before anything is sent; Hydrata refuses fewer than 2 rows, negative rain or flow values and an all-zero rain or flow series.

hold_last_value.description: Set true only when the last value is meant to be held

method.description: One short phrase saying how you got the new numbers. Replaces the earlier account.

name.description: New name (a rainfall polygon binds to its gauge by this exact name)

series_id.description: The time series id (from list_time_series or create_time_series)

series_type.description: New series_type: hyetograph, hydrograph, stage or generic

units.description: New units (must match the series_type, as in create_time_series)

name: update_time_series
title: Correct a time series

annotations.title: Write a project input layer from GeoJSON

description:
Write a project input layer (boundary, friction, inflow, rainfall, building, mesh_region or culvert) from GeoJSON you send in this call.

No file, no key, no upload: the features go in `features`. Hydrata
converts them into the project's grid and puts them in the project's
default layer of that kind, replacing what it held (the old layer is kept,
unlinked). Unlike attach_input_layer there is nothing to poll.

Every feature must be the kind's geometry (lines for boundary, inflow and
culvert; polygons for friction, rainfall, building and mesh_region); a
feature of another geometry refuses the whole write and nothing changes.
A culvert is one two-point line per culvert, Inlet first, then Outlet; its
attributes are the culvert fields (name, shape, width_m, ... see the
culvert guidance), nothing is renamed for you.

Limit: about 150 KB of GeoJSON (a few thousand vertices). A bigger layer
is refused before anything is sent: ask the person to upload it in their
browser with a request_input_upload link instead.

The layer is marked as written by your agent key and is UNREVIEWED until
the user reviews it in their browser. INFLOWS: never invent an inflow
location; take it from the study's files or give the user the ui_url to
draw it.

features.description: A GeoJSON FeatureCollection with every feature of this kind. Coordinates are read as EPSG:4326 (lon/lat) unless the collection declares a `crs` member; Hydrata converts them into the project's grid. Multi* geometries are split into single ones.

kind.description: Which input this is: boundary, friction, inflow, rainfall, building, mesh_region or culvert ('structure' is a deprecated alias of building).

method.description: One short phrase saying how you made these features (e.g. 'traced from the council PDF', 'digitised from the survey CSV'). Shown to the person who reviews the layer.

name: write_input_layer
title: Write a project input layer from GeoJSON
